item.title: Failure to take meaningful steps towards obligations under Development Agreement can’t be protected by S. 14 IBC: Supreme Court
item.description: Invocation of insolvency proceedings or the moratorium under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 cannot become a legal device to indefinitely stall redevelopment. The IBC was never intended to be used as a shield for non-performance at the cost of human rehabilitation. The post Failure to take meaningful steps towards obligations under Development Agreement can’t be protected by S. 14 IBC: Supreme Court appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Foreign Arbitral Awards upholding agreement based on surmises is against public policy & unenforceable: Madras High Court
item.description: The jurisdictional pre-condition for reference to arbitration is the concluded contract between the parties and their intention to refer the dispute to arbitration and in absence of the same, a foreign award would run contrary to the Public Policy of India. The post Foreign Arbitral Awards upholding agreement based on surmises is against public policy & unenforceable: Madras High Court appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: ‘Preliminary enquiry cannot be sole basis for finding guilt or determining punishment’: Rajasthan High Court quashes Constable’s dismissal
item.description: “The fact that the same authority first remanded the matter for enhanced punishment and then, being dissatisfied even with the enhanced penalty of four increments, proceeded suo motu to impose the maximum penalty of dismissal, raises a serious doubt regarding the objectivity and fairness of the process.” The post ‘Preliminary enquiry cannot be sole basis for finding guilt or determining punishment’: Rajasthan High Court quashes Constable’s dismissal appeared first on SCC Times.
